open_order_timing.verdict: 2026-11-23 (13 nuclear stocks, hourly bars Dec 2023-Nov 2026, 9,158 stock-days): the first hour is weak on average (-0.2 to -0.3%) on every gap size except gap-downs of 2%+ (+0.3%, halves disagree). Its low sits 2-3% under the open. Limit buys 1-3% under the open: ~80% of first-hour fills trade at the limit again after 10:30 anyway, and the ~20% that only fill in the first hour are the best trades (+4.5% to +5.2% by the close). So waiting until 10:30 gets no better price and drops the best fills. Kept: orders go in at 9:31 after the open prints (setups the open already broke are dropped first). Not adopted: orders before the bell (they fill at the open even when the stock gaps through support).

support_vs_dipbuy_fills.verdict: 2026-11-23 (10 nuclear stocks, Dec 2023-Nov 2026 hourly for support buys, daily for the dip-buy; $1,000, 25% per trade, max 4 open). Realistic fills (price must trade 0.3% through the order): support buys +0.15%/trade, halves +0.37/-0.07 -> $1,348 (11%/yr, -44%); dip-buy -> $3,036 (47%/yr, -46%). The dip-buy over 2008-2026 with realistic fills and $5+ stocks: 6.7%/yr, worst drop -64%; on the uranium ETF URA (no survivor bias) it lost money (-4.3%/yr). Conclusions: (1) the support buys' paper edge mostly comes from fills that only touched the price; (2) the dip-buy only shone in the 2023-26 bull and on surviving stocks; neither adopted as an upgrade. Added an honest-fill check (fill_check) so the paper record shows P&L without touch-only fills.
